title: Portrait and Witness
premise: Tamsin Nystrom is hired by a dying woman, Ilse Varga, who pays triple to prove that her brother's murder — scheduled, she claims, for the coming solstice — will never happen. The twist: the 'murder' already occurred twenty years ago and was ruled an accident, and the statute of limitations on its cover-up expires in six weeks. Tamsin's photographic memory of a single childhood visit to the Varga house becomes the key: he remembers a portrait that no longer exists, one that hid evidence of what really happened in the boathouse. As Tamsin reopens the case, the family closes ranks around him, and the client's prophecy begins to look less like madness than a confession by proxy. In the end, Tamsin proves the original murder — but discovers Ilse engineered the investigation to force her own daughter, the true killer, to confess before the law could no longer touch her; the case closes not with an arrest but with a truth spoken aloud, and Tamsin gains a found family in the wreckage.
about_author: August Vane is a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing estate inventories and unclaimed inheritances along the Baltic coast. Portrait and Witness is his fourth novel, drawn from a real probate file he was never supposed to read.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. A frail stranger named Ilse Varga walks into Tamsin's shabby office and pays for a future crime that hasn't happened yet: her brother's murder at the summer solstice. Tamsin, unable to resist an impossible case, accepts against his own rules. Emotional beat: wary fascination — the hook of a puzzle that shouldn't exist.

chapters.title: The House That Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. He travels to the decaying Varga estate on the coast and meets the family: brother Anders, alive and bafflingly healthy; niece Katrin, brittle and watchful; the loyal housekeeper Marta. Tamsin notices a pale rectangle on the library wall where a portrait once hung. Emotional beat: creeping wrongness beneath polite hospitality.

chapters.title: A Photograph of Nothing
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin, with a flashback fragment. Digging into the family history, Tamsin finds the official record: Ilse's other brother, Emil, drowned in the boathouse twenty years ago — ruled accidental. But Tamsin's photographic memory snags on a childhood visit: he saw a portrait of Emil, and something about it was off. Emotional beat: the past asserting itself.

chapters.title: Six Weeks
chapters.summary: POV Katrin. Katrin watches the investigator poke at old wounds and quietly begins destroying letters, while her mother Ilse grows weaker and more urgent. Katrin's chapters reveal she knows exactly what happened in the boathouse — and that her mother knows too. Emotional beat: guilt wearing the mask of duty.

chapters.title: The Missing Frame
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. Tracking the removed portrait through an auction house and a restorer's studio, Tamsin learns it was sold years ago by someone with power of attorney — Ilse herself. Why would she hide evidence if she wanted the truth out? Emotional beat: the case turning inside out.

chapters.title: What the Paint Hid
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. Under X-ray, the portrait's underpainting shows Emil standing beside a second figure whose face was painted over — and a date scratched into wet paint: the night before his death. The accident has a witness who was silenced in oil. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into dread as Tamsin realizes the killer is still in the house.

chapters.title: Solstice Eve
chapters.summary: POV alternating Tamsin and Katrin. Storm closes the roads; the family gathers for the midsummer feast, and Ilse announces she is changing her will tonight. Anders rages, Marta burns a letter in the kitchen stove, and Tamsin understands the 'future murder' Ilse paid him to prevent is happening now, in slow motion. Emotional beat: pressure building toward rupture.

chapters.title: The Boathouse Again
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. Climax part one: lured to the boathouse by a forged note, Tamsin confronts the killer — Katrin, who as a teenager struck Emil when he threatened to expose her paternity secret, with Ilse helping bury it ever since. The confrontation turns violent; Marta intervenes, saving Tamsin. Emotional beat: terror and pity entangled.

chapters.title: Portrait and Witness
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. Climax part two: Ilse, dying, stages a final gathering where the restored portrait hangs again. She confesses her own complicity aloud, forcing Katrin to either repeat the silence or break it. Katrin breaks it — confessing before witnesses, surrendering the statute's protection voluntarily. Emotional beat: catharsis through chosen truth over legal necessity.

chapters.title: Closed, For Good
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin, epilogue weeks later. The case closes unconventionally: Katrin awaits trial, Anders leaves the estate to Marta and the village trust, and Ilse dies at peace. Tamsin, invited back for the scattering of ashes, realizes the Vargas — broken, honest, forgiving — have become the family he never had. Emotional beat: quiet, earned belonging.
